title: Nucleation-type criticality with infinite number of free-energy minima beyond mean-field theory
abstract: We study the phase diagram of a three-dimensional Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinski--Moriya interaction under the presence of Potts-like anisotropy. The phase transition between the winding phase and the ferromagnetically ordered phase exhibits a critical phase transition with anomalous features such as critical exponents consistent with that of a first-order transition while maintaining continuity of physical quantities. Furthermore, at the critical point, we see a growing number of free energy local minima, supporting the picture of infinitely many discontinuous transitions forming criticality. Our numerical result unify de Gennes' theory of nucleation-type transitions and Dzyaloshinskii's calculation of chiral magnets by demonstrating that such anomalous criticality can be realized in microscopic models beyond mean-field.
summary: This work analyzes a 3D Heisenberg model with DM interaction to study anomalous critical points. The authors show that the transition can be driven by an infinite number of free-energy minima, leading to critical exponents mimicking first-order behavior while remaining continuous. This unifies theoretical predictions for nucleation-type transitions in microscopic quantum magnets.
main_problem: The paper investigates anomalous critical phase transitions in magnetic models, specifically those exhibiting 'nucleation-type criticality' where infinite free-energy minima drive the transition.
main_result: The study demonstrates that such anomalous criticality, characterized by first-order-like exponents while maintaining physical continuity, can be realized in microscopic models beyond mean-field theory.
method: The research employs extensive numerical simulations, including Monte Carlo methods (Metropolis, overrelaxation) and the multicanonical method, to calculate free energy landscapes and critical exponents.
model_or_system: The system is a three-dimensional Heisenberg model incorporating Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interaction and Potts-like anisotropy, exhibiting transitions between disordered, winding, and ferromagnetic phases.
key_observables: Specific heat ($c$), scaled single-layer magnetic susceptibility ($\chi_{xy}$), $Z_3$ symmetry parameter ($F_3$), and the free energy $f(w)$ as a function of winding number $w$.
important_parameters: The ratio $J_\parallel/J$ controls the nature of the transition, and the system is studied near the Dzyaloshinskii transition temperature ($T_D$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to map the critical behavior to the emergence of multiple, locally stable winding states in the free energy landscape.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram, specific heat, susceptibility, and the structure factor $S(q)$ across different temperature regimes, showing evidence of both continuous and first-order transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the phase diagram, first establishing the model Hamiltonian and simulation techniques, then focusing on the critical behavior by analyzing symmetry parameters and the free energy landscape associated with winding numbers.
why_interesting: The concept of criticality arising from an infinite number of local minima in the free energy is a powerful generalization of standard mean-field descriptions, relevant for understanding complex phase transitions in many-body systems.
